idiom_name: async function consuming an async iterable with for await
implementation_notes: The endpoint is a plain async function: Node's asynchronous iterables (streams, iterator-based clients, async generators) are consumed with for await, the service is awaited inside the loop and the result is sent on the output. That replaces the endpoint class entirely. When the transport only offers an EventEmitter, emitter.on('message', handler) is the fallback, but listeners are called synchronously and their return values are ignored and discarded, so an async listener does not delay the emitter and its rejections escape unless they are caught.
pitfalls: EventEmitter listeners are synchronous and their return value is discarded: a handler that returns a rejected promise reports an unhandled rejection instead of routing the failure to an error channel.

The loop never terminates if the source is never closed, and one loop means serial processing - a slow service stalls every later message; parallel handling needs an explicit bound rather than Promise.all over the stream.
Registering a listener per message (or per request) leaks listeners and triggers MaxListenersExceededWarning; register the activator once per channel.
